spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The discrepancy between a sum and its integral is encoded by a sawtooth term whose bounded periodic primitive makes the Stirling remainder uniformly controllable.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The logarithm of Gamma's product is rearranged into its main terms plus an integral involving [u]-u+1/2; integrating through the bounded primitive of this periodic remainder gives O(1/|z|) uniformly in sectors away from the negative axis.
directed.conceptual_reading: Oscillatory discretization error becomes harmless after one antiderivative, separating universal asymptotic growth from a controlled remainder.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The product formula, a sum-integral remainder, its bounded periodic primitive, and sectorial geometry bridge discrete factorial data to complex uniform asymptotics.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Uniformity excludes a fixed wedge around the negative real axis, where the denominator approaches the Gamma poles and branch cut.
directed.uncertainty: Many displays are severely fragmented; the remainder method and sector are reliable, but exact main terms and derivative errors need scan verification.

supported: The span rewrites log Gamma as its main terms plus an integral of [u]-u+1/2 over u+z.
The primitive of this zero-mean periodic remainder is bounded, and integration by parts changes the denominator to (u+z)^2, yielding O(1/|z|) uniformly for |arg z|<=pi-epsilon.
The conceptual claim that one antiderivative controls oscillatory discretization error is source-grounded.
inference: Calling the remainder a sum-integral discrepancy and emphasizing sectorial geometry are faithful interpretations of the displayed derivation.
unsupported_or_imported: The boundary statement says the denominator approaches the Gamma poles. The span proves only loss of the uniform sectorial estimate as arg z approaches pi; u+z can approach zero along the whole negative axis, not specifically at Gamma poles.
context_or_ocr_risk: Many main-term and corollary displays are severely fragmented, so the candidate is right to reserve exact formulas and derivative errors for scan verification.
revision_instructions: Replace the pole-based rationale in boundary_or_failure with the source-grounded statement that uniformity is proved only for sectors |arg z|<=pi-epsilon because the integral estimate for 1/(u+z)^2 loses a uniform lower bound as z approaches the negative real axis; retain the principal-log/scan caveat without attributing the denominator to Gamma poles.
